Utilizing a diverse array of models InceptionV3, Xception, DenseNet, and CNN .By addressing the urgent need for accurate Tuberculosis diagnosis, this Tuberculosis Detection System contributes to global health efforts, paving the way for improved patient outcomes and disease control strategies. Comparative analysis identifies Xception as the highest overall accuracy of 96.95% with precision, recall, and F1 score values of 97%, 96%, and 97%, respectively. These results highlight the effectiveness of deep learning techniques in achieving high precision and recall crucial for early and reliable Tuberculosis diagnosis. Finally this signifies a leap forward in Tuberculosis detection, highlighting the transformative impact of deep learning in advancing medical diagnostics and public health efforts.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Logistic Regression and Decision Tree Models for Lung Cancer Prediction Using Survey Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the most deadly and ubiquitous forms of cancer globally. Early detection can make a significant difference in survival rates, prognosis, etc. Background The present study compares the performance of logistic regression and decision trees using a survey-based dataset for predicting lung cancer. This dataset has a total of 284 cases with 16 features; behavioral patterns, symptomatic data, and demographic details. Logistic regression is a binary classification algorithm that uses input features to model the probability of lung cancer presence given these input features using for example a sigmoid function. Using Decision Trees can identify significant fields in a dataset while reducing Gini Impurity for models that categorize patients based on feature values. The performance of both models is evaluated according to accuracy, F1-score, precision, and recall measures. From the preliminary results, it looks like the Decision Tree works a little better than the logistic regression model which gets an accuracy of 94%, but this one does with more accuracy (97%). This result emphasizes the inclusion of logistic regression within this context, as it may be able to predict lung cancer with greater accuracy. Additionally, to ensure the generalization and robustness of the model, further investigation and trials will focus on optimizing performance through ensemble approaches, hyperparameter tuning, and cross-validation. This comparative analysis demonstrates the effectiveness of machine learning techniques in developing prediction models for early lung cancer detection, an important step toward a quick and appropriate intervention.

articleTitle: Enhancing Operational Efficiency and Security in Multi-Sectioned Businesses with Edge AI through Real-Time Analytics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)
abstract: The goal of this project is to disrupt the way businesses monitor their operations by integrating IoT and machine learning to gain a deeper understanding of customer behavior and improve operational efficiency. Traditional surveillance systems create lots of data to store and analyze, but they do not provide actionable intelligence. CCTV cameras and edge devices strategically placed throughout a facility capture real-time footage, identify visitor movement patterns, and represent critical heat zones on a heat map. This data-driven process enhances resource allocation, enhances customer experience, and enables proactive improvements in operational workflow. Edge devices enable real-time anomaly detection, such as theft or staff sitting, without compromising privacy, as the device retains all information and performs all processing locally. Our next-gen solution provides businesses with an all-inclusive monitoring system that solves today's most pressing security and operational issues, ultimately delivering better business results.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Model for Sentimental Analysis of Amazon Reviews
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)
abstract: The goal of this project is to draw a deeper understanding of the subjective nature behind online product reviews, largely by examining a large dataset received from Amazon that contains numerous star ratings and comments. Since there is such a massive amount of data on the Amazon platform, it was perfect for the analysis. Our methodology is platform-agnostic and can be easily extended to other comparable datasets from other web platforms with comparable guarantees in achieving wide applicability. Our primary motivation is improving the dependability of online shopping. Since product reviews are currently widely used by many consumers as guides in making decisions to buy products, such reviews ought to be fair representations of the actual dependability and quality of the products. The goal of our effort is to identify patterns in the language and ratings of such reviews that would directly reflect the real customer sentiment and also the reliability of the product. Our approach has yielded already a rate of about 92%, which shows it has the potential greatly to raise the legitimacy of online reviews. We'd like to make our customers feel more confident and better equipped with information to make better and safer purchases on a website like Amazon and others. In the final analysis, we strive to make online shopping for our customers worldwide safer and more trustworthy.

articleTitle: Adaptable Individualized Investment Recommendation System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)
abstract: Internetization has played a massive role in the rapid development and growth of the financial investment industry. Due to the rapid development, there is a demand for more financial knowledge services to help make well-informed investments. Accessing and conducting investments through online financial platforms has made the field highly accessible. This has made the investment recommendation system a popular research area. Personalized recommendations will help the user make investments that are safe for their financial situation and also suit their particular needs and interests. This work proposes a method where investment recommendations are given based on three key factors. The user interest sectors, risk appetite-based clustering, and market sentiment of the stock. These factors will be calculated by the use of Lasso regression, SVM, stepwise regression, generalized boosted regression, random forest, ridge regression and fuzzy clustering. Based on these three factors, the proposed method results in investment recommendations made for users that are personalized to the specific user. This allows existing investors to gain new opportunities and new investors to start investing with lower amount of risk using the information available.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Sleep Well Monitor: Enhancing Health Through Snore Detection and Vital Signs Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)
abstract: During sleep, airflow partially blocked in the throat can cause tissues to vibrate, leading to snoring sound most people experience at some point but one that can indicate underlying health concerns. Persistent snoring, often associated with sleep apnea, can impact sleep quality and health. This paper introduces a novel, user-friendly snoring detection device designed for at-home use, with the ability to distinguish snore and non-snore sounds by analyzing complex patterns in sound signals through chaotic features such as entropy and Largest Lyapunov Exponents (LLEs). In addition to sound, the device integrates sensors for temperature, vibration, and body movement, allowing a comprehensive assessment of sleep health factors. This approach provides a full picture of how elements likesleep position, movement, and snoring patterns interact, offering users actionable insights into their sleep quality. By giving early warnings of potential sleep issues, this system aims to empower users to manage snoring and its effects, aiding both in-homemonitoring and broader sleep research. The ultimate goal of this tool is to promote healthier sleep habits through data-driven, real-time feedback on snoring and sleep quality.

articleTitle: Seagrass Species Recognition using Generalized Transfer Learning Resnet CNN Synergized with Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)
abstract: Seagrasses are vital marine plants that provide essential habitats for aquatic species and play a critical role in maintaining healthy coastal ecosystems. However, manually identifying seagrass species are challenging to classify due to underwater image constraints such as low visibility, varying lighting, and distortion which complicates traditional classification methods. This study primarily addresses the challenge of creating a robust, automated system to overcome limitations in underwater imaging. To optimize this, we propose a hybrid system to classify distinct seagrass species from underwater imagery captured by drones, autonomous underwater vehicles, and manned submersibles. Initially, features are automatically extracted from seagrass images using a pre-trained deep convolutional neural network (CNN). Subsequently, machine learning algorithms categorize these images into distinct species. We conducted experiments using two distinct architectures. In first experiment we synergized ResNet-50 CNN with Support Vector Machine (SVM) algorithm and in the second model utilized the standard ResNet-101 CNN with SVM for classification. Our experiments, which considered both small and large datasets, showed that the ResNet-50 CNN synergized with SVM yielded the highest accuracy of about 99.15%. The hybrid approach of ResNet-50 and SVM proved highly effective seagrass classification due to SVM’s robust handling of extracted features. This combination offers a promising, reliable tool for seagrass identification, aiding environmental monitoring and conservation efforts.

Author Keywords: Hybrid CNN and Machine Learning Model

articleTitle: Real-Time Eye State Detection Using Deep Learning for Blink and Dry Eye Diagnosis using Smart Phone
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)
abstract: Inspection of blinks and real-time recognition of eye states is crucial for diagnosing ophthalmologic symptoms: dry eye, drowsiness, fatigue, etc. This work presents a new eye state recognition method using a VGG16-based model with deep learning. The model is trained on 1234 training photos and 218 test images with equal numbers of closed and open in a balanced dataset to detect eye conditions accurately. To increase the robustness of the model, data augmentation techniques like random rotation, zooming, and horizontal flip are applied to training data. The model learns to fine-tune after transfer learning on the pre-trained VGG16 and several dense layers make improvements on feature extraction. Experimental results show that the proposed model has achieved an excellent accuracy of 98% for both closed and open-eye classification. Similarly, we can attain over 97% precision, recall, and F1 for both classes. The high throughput of the system to obtain blink patterns shows how important it is as a powerful tool for real-time eye monitoring, such as dry eye detection and sleep alertness systems installation. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of deep learning models in medical and safety-critical domains, showcasing superior generalization abilities across various test environments.

articleTitle: Performance Metrics and Accuracy Assessment of Machine Learning Models for Crop Recommendation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electronic Systems and Intelligent Computing (ICESIC)
abstract: In this work, five machine-learning techniques are compared on crop recommendation. The Random Forest model achieved an accuracy of 99.09%, with both precision and recall at 99.19%. In comparison, the Decision Tree reached an accuracy of 98.33%, but demonstrated higher precision and the Support Vector Machine (SVM) also performed well but slightly less accurately than the Random Forest, with an accuracy of 97.27%. KNN showed an accuracy of 96.06% and performed well, but the ensemble approaches surpassed it. Despite being simpler and more interpretable, Logistic Regression had the worst accuracy of 95.91%. Results: These results indicate strong performance of ensemble methods on complex classification problems. Results were consistent across Decision Tree and SVM while comparable but notably weaker in KNN and Logistic Regression. The comparative analysis highlights the primacy of Random Forest on resilience and precision with an affirmation that simpler models such as Logistic Regression still have high utility in certain circumstances. Future research could focus on fine-tuning model hyperparameters, and exploring additional methodologies to improve classification performance.
